reasoning_traces.think:
The interception model operates as a Poisson process with rate parameter λ·p_worthy·p_convert. The key insight is that while individual game INTs are noisy, the long-run average follows this deterministic formula. The 52.3% conversion is treated as a fixed constant derived from league-wide data, implying no situational variation. This creates a dualism: the deterministic component (λ·p_worthy) is based on measurable QB behavior, whereas the stochastic conversion is a black-box assumption. The model fails when pressure or context-sensitive factors are introduced, as these are explicitly vetoed. The system thus enforces a clean separation between predictable volume and unpredictable luck. The veto on sack projections reflects the same principle—pressure generation is sticky but conversion to sacks is random, making projections unreliable. Volume adjustments correct for sample bias but do not alter the core probabilistic structure. All primitives are grounded in empirical ratios and literature-backed assumptions.
